turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me a second, this thing's installing an update. Mrs Kapoor? Have a seat. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing, if I'm honest. My daughter fusses over me.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm her daughter, I live with her. She slid down twice and I wasn't going to ignore it.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Slid down? Say that again, I was on the wrong screen.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Twice. Once in the kitchen, once getting to the bathroom. She says it wasn't a fall, she slid.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It wasn't a fall. My legs went soft and I sort of sat down. I didn't hurt myself.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you black out at all? Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I never blacked out, and there's no chest pain. I'm not ill.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about dizziness? Does the room spin, or do you go faint?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't get dizzy. Never have.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, bear with me, it's logged me out. Typical. So you're saying no dizziness?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, when I get up out of the armchair it goes a bit swimmy. A second or two. Not proper spinning. I hold on and it passes.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's every time she stands up quickly. She grabs the doorframe. And both times she went down she was white as a sheet for a minute.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): It passes if I hold the chair. I don't see the panic. I had a biscuit and got on with the crossword.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the swimmy feeling start? I need something for the notes.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't give you a date. Since Diwali, or after. Or last winter, or the one before. It's all a blur.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She won't be pinned down on the dizzy bit. The first slide was about three weeks ago, the second was last Thursday, after tea.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, three weeks or three months? The cursor jumped.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three weeks. Not months. And last Thursday for the second one.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. I don't sit about counting them.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines. The list on here is from last year and I don't trust it. What do you actually take?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A few blood pressure tablets, and something for sleep. I hardly take anything.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Three for her blood pressure every morning, and a sleeping tablet at night.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Slowly, please, I'm typing. Start with the amlodipine.

[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amlodipine ten milligrams in the morning, ramipril five milligrams in the morning, and bendroflumethiazide two point five milligrams in the morning. Zopiclone three point seven five at bedtime for sleep, and the first three are all for her blood pressure.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): The zopiclone I only take if I'm lying there awake. Not every night.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's meant to take it nightly. Some weeks the strip's empty, though, so I honestly don't know.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the sleeping tablet as it is today. Anything else, aspirin, a chemist buy?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just those. Morning ones with breakfast, regular as clockwork.
[SEG0030] person_4 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. I've done the lying and standing blood pressures.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Go on, and slowly. I'll put them in the wrong boxes otherwise.
[SEG0032] person_4 (NURSE): Lying, one hundred and forty-eight over eighty-two, pulse sixty-eight. Standing, after one minute, one hundred and eighteen over seventy, pulse eighty-four.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Standing one eighteen over seventy, pulse eighty-four? Lying one forty-eight over eighty-two, pulse sixty-eight?
[SEG0034] person_4 (NURSE): That's the one. She said the swimmy feeling came on as she stood, and it eased once she kept still. She didn't go down.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): See? It eased. You're all making a meal of it.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still a drop of thirty on the systolic when you stand. One forty-eight down to one eighteen.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): So that's why she's ending up on the floor?

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think so. My impression is postural hypotension, her pressure falling when she stands, from the blood pressure tablets. Not a definite diagnosis until we see how she does on a lower dose, but it fits the sliding and the swimmy head.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I've had high blood pressure for donkey's years. That's hardly news.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, the hypertension is ongoing. The lying reading is still up, we're not ignoring it.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Cross me off, then, and I'll get the bus.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not yet. I want to change one tablet. Amlodipine down from ten milligrams to five milligrams, once each morning. Ramipril and bendroflumethiazide stay as they are.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Does she start the five tonight, or tomorrow?
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tomorrow morning. I'll send the prescription through. Take today's ten as normal.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Five milligrams sounds a bit feeble. I'm not keeling over, you know.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's a small step down, and the other two are still there. Get up in stages. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand, and don't rush for the phone.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She is up the second the kettle boils. I'll have to nag.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not rush. I walk perfectly well, thank you.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): And don't let yourself dry out, it makes the drop worse. Tea is fine, within reason.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Could the zopiclone be adding to it? The bathroom one was after tea, though, not in the night.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): It might be contributing, but I'm only changing the amlodipine today. Leave the zopiclone dose alone. We can revisit it if the standing pressure is still falling next time.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. I like a proper night's sleep.
[SEG0053] person_4 (NURSE): Do you want another standing pressure, or am I done?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're done, thanks. No more obs today. I'll check it again when she's back.
[SEG0055] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And if she slides before then, do I ring you?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. If she slides again, blacks out, or the swimmy feeling isn't settling, come back sooner, don't wait the fortnight. Otherwise I'll see you in a fortnight.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight. I'm still saying I slid. I did not fall. Put that down if you must.
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We'll get the prescription on the way out. Come on, Mum, mind the step.
